1. Outcome and exact scope

There are two explicit positive RC impedances, with the same positive series
inductance and the same 19-mode positive RC baseline, that satisfy every real
and imaginary component of the supplied 58-point EIS row to strictly less than
0.1 mOhm. Their Q_1000 values lie respectively in

  [187.72905369456885, 187.72905369456890] mOhm,
  [266.16089938984990, 266.16089938985000] mOhm.

Thus they straddle the 200 mOhm decision. Unlike the source packet's original
countermodels, this pair also remains hard for EVERY bounded-current waveform
over a short experiment, including multisine, binary, chirp, and adaptive input
selection under the contract below. The proof does not depend on a grid bound.

For a 10 s experiment with |i| <= Imax, their output voltage separation is at
most Imax times 0.030362450172885497 mOhm at every instant. If the additional
voltage observation error obeys |e(t)| <= epsilon_V and

  eta := epsilon_V / Imax >= 0.01518122508644275 mOhm,

the full voltage record can be identical under both models. Consequently every
Q_1000 estimator has worst-case absolute error at least 39.21592284764051 mOhm,
and every binary classifier of these two models can be forced to err. This
remains true when the estimator is told the entire baseline and exact hard pair.

This eta is a NEW SYMBOLIC TIME-DOMAIN ERROR INTERFACE. It is not inferred from
the EIS error parameter, an instrument specification, or a measured pulse trace.
Numerical eta examples below are hypothetical. Both current and voltage are
incremental linear-response quantities with known zero initial state.
Here epsilon_V is expressed in mV and Imax in A, so their ratio has units mOhm.
If epsilon_V is expressed in V, eta in mOhm is 1000*epsilon_V/Imax.

The EIS premise remains the source's exploratory restricted model: 58 points
from 0.01 through 904.7 Hz, and a deterministic 0.1 mOhm component box. The full
70-point spectrum rejects a positive RC fit at this error: its real-part
ordering violation forces at least 0.515 mOhm uniform error. Nothing here repairs
that rejection or validates finite-amplitude, state-dependent battery behavior.
Existing pseudo-open-circuit and pulse data are additional information to which
this lower bound is not automatically applicable.

source_excerpts.text:
3. Sharp waveform discrimination under peak and slew limits

First assume only |i(t)| <= Imax on [0,H]. Since g is nonnegative,

  |Delta v(t)| <= Imax*integral_0^t g(v)dv
               = Imax*d(t) <= Imax*d(H).                  (4)

The constant pulse i(t)=Imax attains (4) at H. Hence d(H) is the EXACT induced
L-infinity to L-infinity separation per unit maximum current for this pair on
[0,H]. This is exact optimality for this pair, not a claim that a constant pulse
is universally optimal for all possible RC identification problems.

Now impose a physically finite rise rate: i(0)=0, |i(t)| <= Imax, and
|i'(t)| <= Imax/rho almost everywhere, where rho>0 is the minimum full-scale
rise time. Any such input satisfies

  |i(t)| <= Imax*p_rho(t),  p_rho(t)=min(t/rho,1).

The nonnegative envelope i_*(t)=Imax*p_rho(t) is admissible and pointwise dominates
every admissible absolute input. Therefore it maximizes the absolute separation
at every time simultaneously. Integration by parts in (3) yields its output
separation at H:

  S(H,rho) = Imax*K(H,rho),
  K(H,rho) = (1/rho)*integral_max(0,H-rho)^H d(v)dv.         (5)

K is nonnegative and strictly increasing for H>0. The exact optimal waveform is
a maximum allowed ramp followed by a full-scale plateau. Formula (5) remains
valid when H<rho, when the waveform has not reached the plateau. The limit
rho=0 is K(H,0)=d(H).

A finite return ramp AFTER the last observation can be appended and charged
separately. The theorem's clock ends at the last observation; it does not count
subsequent reset time as zero. If a charge-balanced final input, a final zero
current at H, an energy bound, thermal constraints, or smaller admissible current
is required, the feasible input set is smaller. The lower bound survives; this
particular exact optimal waveform and its upper bound need not remain feasible.

4. Indistinguishability, including adaptive measurements

Fix a deterministic finite sequential strategy: each chosen input segment may
depend on all previous observed voltage values and on the already supplied EIS
row. Inputs satisfy the same peak/slew constraints. The observer may read the
whole resulting path, so the lower bound also covers any finite sampling plan.
For a continuous-time feedback formulation, require a well-posed causal closed
loop for every model in the convex segment between Z_- and Z_+, including the
midpoint.

source_excerpts.text:
Append-only clarification to frozen PROOF.txt, section 4 and equation (8).
15 October 2026. The frozen files remain unchanged.

The main lower bound and the sharp segment minimax equality are proved for
DETERMINISTIC finite sequential strategies, or deterministic well-posed causal
policies, with arbitrary bounded deterministic observation error. This class is
already sufficient for the stated all-waveform comparison and exact ramp probe.

The sentence about a randomized strategy's equal-prior classification error
being at least one half uses a stronger explicit noise-adversary contract:

  The bounded corruption may be causal and may react to the applied current
  history; it need not be an oblivious fixed function selected before the
  investigator's random seed. It does not need access to that private seed or
  to future random choices.

Indeed, under actual model Z_theta the causal corruption

  e_theta(t) = (1/2-theta)*(g*i)(t)

makes the observed output equal to the midpoint model's output, for every
realized current history. The convolution uses only past applied current and
has magnitude at most the stated bound for the selected hard parameters.
Consequently, conditional on the investigator's own random seed, the observed
transcript is still independent of which endpoint is true. Equal-prior binary
classification error is then at least one half. The same argument extends the
segment minimax lower bound to randomized strategies under this current-reactive
adversarial error model.

No randomized lower bound against an OBLIVIOUS fixed-noise adversary is claimed.
No independent Gaussian, white-noise, stochastic calibration, or repeated-sample
noise law is assumed or ruled out. Such assumptions define different problems.
In summaries, either say deterministic strategies and arbitrary bounded error,
or state the causal current-reactive noise contract when including randomized
strategies. Do not silently combine these two quantifier orders.
